procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires the factory to be registered outside a free zone, with a MoIAT industrial licence and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added, before applying for a certificate.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The issuing authority requires the application to include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product, and each item must qualify separately.

The Ministry of Foreign Trade's e-service requires the applicant to log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the Certificate of Origin for India service, fill in the application form, upload proof of factory registration and the commercial invoice (and for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice), and pay the fee online.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 10 to AED 200 depending on invoice value.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade's e-service requires the applicant to submit the application and print the approved certificate after approval, or correct the return with comments.
The competent authority issues the certificate prior to, at, or within five working days of export; it is valid for twelve months from issue and covers only one import.

The exporter must ship goods directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. Third-party invoicing is allowed if the exporter indicates it.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020, including which origin criterion is claimed.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years from the end of the calendar year of issue.

caveats.note: The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
No usable shipment value was provided, so only rates are given; the actual saving depends on the shipment value.
Mansha interprets '+' in the rule as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+'.

The terms 'direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement, and it is unclear whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate; confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically; the India-specific certificate page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources, not the official text.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
The certificate fee range is AED 10 to AED 200; the exact fee depends on the invoice value in AED.
